title: "L'Estat du Roy de Navarre et de son party en France", BL Harley MS 1582 ff. 263-264 (DECODE R8505)

steps.what: Checked the catalogue's two records: R8501 (Harley 1582 ff. 71-72) proved to be a Stafford 1586 despatch already read in the sibling target harley1582r8500 from its own f.72r decipherment; only R8505 was open.
Fetched the four full-resolution R8505 images with the DECODE session cookie.

Identified the document from its clear text: the French memoir 'L'Estat du Roy de Navarre & de son party en France', written after 1580, on Navarre's standing, places, gentlemen and alliances. DECODE had no title, no date, no author and gave the language as English.
Searched for the memoir in print and in the Calendars of State Papers Foreign 1583-86, and for a graphic-sign Navarre key in DECODE and Tomokiyo's tables.

Transcribed every cipher run on all four sides (3,630 sign tokens, 56 sign names) against a shared sign chart; lines slope by a full line-height across the page, so runs were followed in overlapping band crops.
IC 0.0398 over 3,630 tokens and Sukhotin's vowel test: consistent with a homophonic alphabet of about 50 signs, not with a syllabary (the commonest sign carries 8.7% of the text).
Homophonic annealing with a 1530-1600 French LM (order 4/5, no spaces) and a unigram-frequency penalty, up to 20 restarts x 400k moves, whole text and page by page.
Variant allowing each sign to stand for a letter, a common syllable, a double or a null.

Language control: the same anneal under English, Spanish, Italian and 17th-c. French models reaches the same score as the French despatch model (about -2.9/char against -1.9 for real text), so no language fits and no key was found.

outcome.fraction_read_source: ciphertext.txt: 3630 cipher tokens, none given a value
outcome.notes: The document is identified and transcribed for the first time; the cipher is not broken. The most likely obstacles are the sign-level transcription error rate and the possibility that the key mixes letters with syllables, doubles and nulls, as a 1583 letter to Segur describes for Navarre's ciphers of these years.

prior.where: none found on the DECODE record, in the volume's other records (R8498-R8506), or in print/calendars

human: supplied the DECODE login cookie (stored in the repository) and the target
